Brown Act
Agendas are drafted to accurately state what the legislative body is being asked to consider.
The legislative body can take action on "all items" listed on the agenda and be in compliance
with the open meeting laws. Under the Brown Act, no action may be taken on a matter unless
it is listed on the agenda, or unless certain emergency or special circumstances exist. The
governing body may direct staff to investigate and/or schedule certain matters for
consideration at a future meeting.

   Parks & Recreation Commission
  Regular Meeting Minutes
  July 9, 2026

CALL TO ORDER - Chair Flores called the meeting to order at 7:01 p.m.

FLAG SALUTE – by Vice Chair Ruiz

ROLL CALL - by Noemi Aguilera, Secretary
Present: Chair Flores, Vice Chair Ruiz, and Commissioner Trujillo; Secretary Esquivel and Commissioner
Pelayo had excused absences.
Staff: Director of Parks & Recreation Tina De La Rosa, Parks Superintendent Glenn Massey and Recreation
Coordinator Franklin Arroyo.

APPROVAL OF MEETING MINUTES
Regular Meeting Minutes of December 11, 2025, February 12, 2026 and April 9, 2026.
Recommended Motion: Motion to approve the minutes as presented.
M/S/C: Vice Chair Ruiz/Commissioner Trujillo

PUBLIC COMMENTS
Recognized: Johnny Hoang, Recreation Leader IV with the Parks and Recreation Department - Highlighted
four upcoming community fitness events and programs. These include a Fun Run on July 18, a 12-week, a
Weight Loss Challenge beginning July 20, a Sound Bath on July 25, and a Survivor Challenge on July 27.
Residents interested in participating can register or obtain additional information at the South Gate Sports
Center.

Recognized: A Zoom call from Mario Dominguez SG Resident - Expressed strong dissatisfaction with the
City Council’s decision to set the Utility User Tax at 8%. He also criticized the City Manager and Council for
previously choosing smaller budget reductions. Finally, announced plans to advocate for placing council
term limits on the November ballot, expressing concern about long-serving council members and the lack
of limits on their tenure.

OPEN SESSION ITEMS

1. REVIEW OF HAS ANNUAL REPORT FOR 2025
Recommended Motion: Motion to receive and file.
M/S/C: Commissioner Trujillo/Vice Chair Ruiz
Director De La Rosa introduced Katherine Villanueva, Director of Early Childhood Education Programs for
the HSA who reviewed this item; a discussion ensued. Vice Chair Ruiz asked if there are qualifications
required to which Director Villanueva explained. Chair Flores expressed gratitude for the program.

2. ANNUAL REVIEW OF PARKS & REC MASTER PLAN – ORAL REPORT
Recommended Motion: Motion to receive and file.
M/S/C: Vice Chair Ruiz/Commissioner Trujillo

Director De La Rosa reviewed this item. Chair Flores asked on challenges in completing projects due to
budget cuts; a discussion ensued.

Parks & Recreation Commission Minutes of July 9, 2026  Page 1 of 3
  4
 Recognized: A Zoom call from Mario Dominguez SG Resident - Discussed the Girls Club House Master Plan,
which includes several development options. He also encouraged future use of CDBG funds to address
interior improvements. Additionally, he criticized the longstanding lack of a completed master plan for
Hollydale Regional Park, describing it as a sign of ongoing neglect and urging the Parks Director to prioritize
its completion in future years.

DIRECTOR'S REPORT / CALENDAR OF EVENTS
Director De La Rosa: Provided an update on recent community events, programs, and facility
improvements. Highlights included a successful Summer Kickoff, a well-attended Men’s Health Fair, and
the ongoing Parks Make Life Better Month, which offers daily activities for residents of all ages and has
seen growing participation.
The department also reported on a successful Fourth of July celebration, with carnival proceeds helping
fund the fireworks, and recognized the contributions of Parks and Recreation, Police, and Public Works
staff in ensuring the event ran smoothly.
At Circle Park, repairs are underway to address stolen water infrastructure, cracked pickleball courts,
basketball court surface damage, and drainage issues at the futsal courts. Additional updates included the
installation and testing of a new scoreboard at the Swim Stadium, replacement of aging commercial ice
machines at department facilities, and community soccer activities and World Cup watch parties held in
partnership with local organizations.

Recreation Coordinator Arroyo: The Teen Center is offering several upcoming excursions, including trips
to Six Flags, Universal CityWalk, and Raging Waters, with spots still available. Upcoming community events
include Concerts in the Park on July 30, featuring Los del Momento, a DJ, and vendors; the third annual
Family Camp Night on August 1, which is supported through sponsorships; and a Senior Dance on
September 11 for residents age 55 and older.

Superintendent Massey: Parks maintenance staff are actively managing increased summer-season
demands, including additional irrigation to maintain turf following the carnival and during hot weather.
Staff are also monitoring irrigation functionality and addressing increased restroom usage.

PARKS & RECREATION COMMISSION SUB-COMMITTEE REPORTS
Vice Chair Ruiz: Expressed appreciation for the Fourth of July event and for the many city classes that her
child attends. Is hopeful for UUT passing to continue to have this event for the coming years.

Commissioner Trujillo: Emphasized the size of the event and how important it is to the community.

Chair Flores: Spoke on the tradition of the annual fireworks show at the park. Encouraged Director De La
Rosa to seek alternate funding to help fund these events. Grateful for the staff that assists in the various
classes throughout the parks.

REQUEST FOR ITEMS ON FUTURE AGENDAS – Chair Flores mentioned having an October meeting before
the election to educate the community on possible impacts should UUT not pass.

ADJOURNMENT - At 7:47 p.m. Chair Flores asked for a motion to adjourn.
M/S/C: Commissioner Trujillo/Vice Chair Ruiz

   Parks & Recreation Commission
  Regular Meeting Minutes
  August 13, 2026

CALL TO ORDER - Chair Flores called the meeting to order at 7:04 p.m.

FLAG SALUTE - by Commissioner Pichardo

ROLL CALL - by Noemi Aguilera, Secretary
Present: Chair Flores, Vice Chair Ruiz, Secretary Esquivel, Commissioner Trujillo and Commissioner
Pichardo.
Staff: Director of Parks & Recreation Tina De La Rosa, Parks Superintendent Glenn Massey, Grounds
Supervisor Daniel Rodriguez and Recreation Manager James Markel.

PUBLIC COMMENTS
Recognized: A Zoom call from Mario Dominguez SG resident – Expressed frustration with the city’s
repeated budget presentations. They also raised concerns about the city’s zoning and planning decisions,
particularly the placement of Circle Park and Urban Orchard Park within heavy-manufacturing zones.
Finally, criticized the City Council and commissioners for not supporting term limits.

Recognized: A Zoom call from Gil Hurtado SG Resident - Welcomed Xochilt Pichardo to the Commission
and expressed appreciation for the dedication of the Commission’s longtime community volunteers. They
also recognized city staff for their efforts in delivering programs, securing funding, and supporting local
youth and senior organizations. He concluded by thanking everyone for their continued service to the
community.

OPEN SESSION ITEMS

1. REVIEW OF RECREATION PROGRAMS 4TH QUARTER FY 2025/26
Recommended Motion: Motion to receive and file.
M/S/C: Secretary Esquivel/Commissioner Trujillo
Director De La Rosa introduced Recreation Manager James Markel, who reviewed this item. He went into
details on how the fourth quarter saw strong participation and growth across all recreation, a discussion
ensued. Vice Chair Ruiz thanked staff for all they do in these programs and stated they are of value to the
community.

2. REVIEW OF GROUNDS & FACILITY MAINTENANCE 4TH QUARTER FY 2025/26
Recommended Motion: Motion to receive and file.
M/S/C: Vice Chair Ruiz/Commissioner Trujillo
Grounds Supervisor Daniel Rodriguez reviewed this item; a discussion ensued.

Recognized: A Zoom call from Mario Dominguez SG Resident - Requested an update on the condition of
the trees at Urban Orchard Park following the heat wave, including whether any trees have been lost. They
also asked about the city’s plans and timeline for installing the French drain at Circle Park, including
whether the project is anticipated for the current or next fiscal year.

Parks & Recreation Commission Minutes of August 13, 2026  Page 1 of 3
  7
 3. UPDATE ON PARKS & RECREATION DEPARTMENT MAJOR PROJECTS
Recommended Motion: Motion to receive and file.
M/S/C: Secretary Esquivel/Commissioner Trujillo
Director De La Rosa reviewed this item, a discussion ensued. Vice Chair Ruiz asked about additional funding
to complete certain projects. Recreation Manager Markel explained the different grants that the
department can use for these projects.

Recognized: A Zoom call from Mario Dominguez SG resident – Requested that new city buses include bike
racks to improve access to East Side parks and provide safer transportation options for residents. They also
expressed concern about delays in completing park-related projects funded through Community
Development Block Grant funds and the potential loss or reallocation of funds. He emphasized the need for
timely project delivery and stronger oversight to prevent future funding losses.

DIRECTOR'S REPORT / CALENDAR OF EVENTS
Director De La Rosa: The department reported a successful inaugural Summer Park Program in July,
offering free daily activities that grew to approximately 100 children per day. Staff were recognized for
effectively utilizing existing resources while providing diverse programming for children, teens, and
families.
Additional community events were also successful, including the July 30 Concert in the Park, which
attracted approximately 350–400 attendees, and the August 1 Family Camp Night, which included 40
registered families. Staff were commended for their commitment and adaptability, particularly during the
summer heat. Upcoming activities include an Eco Garden Workshop, a Movie in the Park on August 28, and
the annual golf tournament on August 30.

PARKS & RECREATION COMMISSION SUB-COMMITTEE REPORTS
Secretary Esquivel: Praised the July events, noting that the activities appeared engaging and well received
based on the community posts. She commended staff for their efforts and the success of the programs.

Vice Chair Ruiz: Expressed appreciation for the department’s programs, noting their continued
improvement and strong staff performance. She also suggested partnering with the Kiwanis for monthly
park cleanups and offered to explore opportunities for community volunteers to assist with maintenance.

Commissioner Pichardo: Expressed appreciation for the department’s hard work and dedication,
highlighting the important role parks and recreation facilities have played in the community.

Commissioner Trujillo: Praised the July park events, noting that they provided a positive summer
experience for their child and quickly gained popularity through community word-of-mouth. He
commended staff for the program’s success and strong community participation.

Chair Flores: Commended the team for its strong collaboration, cross-training, and ability to leverage staff
experience and institutional knowledge. He also recognized the team’s creativity in maximizing existing
staffing resources, avoiding unnecessary overtime, and working within budget constraints. Encouraged
continued teamwork and collaboration across departments and emphasized the value of engaging
community organizations, such as Kiwanis and other local groups, for volunteer support and event
assistance. He offered continued support and encouraged the team to reach out whenever needed.

 REQUEST FOR ITEMS ON FUTURE AGENDAS – Chair Flores asked about having an October meeting to
discuss potential impacts on Parks & Recreation department should UUT pass or not.

ADJOURNMENT - At 8:21 p.m. Chair Flores asked for a motion to adjourn.
M/S/C: Vice Chair Ruiz/Secretary Esquivel

Respectfully submitted:

Cynthia Esquivel, Secretary

  Regular Meeting Minutes
  September 10, 2026

CALL TO ORDER - Chair Flores called the meeting to order at 7:01 p.m.

FLAG SALUTE - by Commissioner Ruiz

ROLL CALL - by Noemi Aguilera, Secretary
Present: Chair Flores, Vice Chair Ruiz, Secretary Esquivel and Commissioner Pichardo; Commissioner
Trujillo arrived late at 7:03 pm.
Staff: Director of Parks & Recreation Tina De La Rosa, Parks Superintendent Glenn Massey, and Recreation
Manager Nicki Salazar.

APPROVAL OF MEETING MINUTES
Regular Meeting Minutes of May 14, 2026.
Recommended Motion: Motion to approve the minutes as presented.
M/S/C: Secretary Esquivel/Vice Chair Ruiz

PUBLIC COMMENTS
Recognized: A Zoom call from Mario Dominguez SG resident – Proposed hosting a City Council candidate
forum in the auditorium on either October 10 or 17, from 4–6 p.m. He also encouraged continued outreach
to local community organizations for volunteer support and emphasized the importance of civic
engagement.

Commissioner Eric Trujillo came in during this part of the meeting.

OPEN SESSION ITEMS

1. ANNUAL REVIEW OF FEE WAIVERS FY 2025/26
Recommended Motion: To receive and file and forward the attached report to the City Council.
M/S/C: Vice Chair Ruiz/Commissioner Trujillo
Director De La Rosa reviewed this item, a discussion ensued.

Recognized: A Zoom call from Mario Dominguez SG Resident - Requested clarification on whether the
food bank is held at Hollydale Regional Park or Hollydale Community Park. He also noted that the similar
park names can cause confusion and suggested renaming Hollydale Community Park for greater clarity.

DIRECTOR'S REPORT / CALENDAR OF EVENTS
Director De La Rosa: Reported that cooling centers were opened for two consecutive days due to extreme
heat exceeding 100 degrees, with the Sports Center remaining available through the evening. She also
explained the removal of trees in front of the Senior Center due to expanding roots damaging the brick
walkway and creating a significant trip-and-fall hazard for seniors. Staff are working to restore the area,
maintain an alternative shaded outdoor space, and explore temporary shade structures until new
landscaping and trees can be established. Safety was emphasized as the primary reason for the tree
removal.

Parks & Recreation Commission Minutes of September 10, 2026  Page 1 of 2
  10
 Recreation Manager Salazar: The Recreation Department reported strong participation in recent programs
despite budget constraints, including the Movie in the Park, Concerts, and ongoing recreation classes. Staff
members were recognized for taking on leadership roles and successfully planning and coordinating
events.
Upcoming activities include a sold-out Senior Dance, pickleball social, health and wellness workshop, Teen
Center anniversary celebration, volleyball and basketball tournaments, and an Art Walk. The Senior Center
is also expanding programming through an AARP-funded Digital Connection Lab and new “Doc Talk”
educational sessions covering topics such as technology, fraud prevention, health, and fall prevention.
Also, there’s a new, fully funded overnight Catalina Island camping opportunity for up to 12 local youth in
grades 4–12, with a parent information meeting scheduled for next week.

Superintendent Massey: A large Canary Island pine on Southern Avenue was removed after it sustained
damage, potentially related to nearby fencing and concrete work. During the summer months, staff are
primarily focused on irrigation, landscaping, and maintaining parks as clean, safe, and enjoyable spaces
rather than undertaking major projects.

PARKS & RECREATION COMMISSION SUB-COMMITTEE REPORTS
Commissioner Trujillo: Asked what the age requirement for senior programming is, expressed gratitude for
classes educating seniors on technology.

Vice Chair Ruiz: Emphasized the importance of promoting the City’s wide range of programs and services,
noting that many residents may not be aware of the resources available for youth, teens, adults, and
seniors. Highlighted the Senior Center in particular as a source of important and much-needed services for
the community. Expressed gratitude to maintenance staff for upkeep of parks despite the heat.

Chair Flores: Acknowledged the impact of reduced programming this summer, noting that fewer concerts
and movie nights limited opportunities for community engagement. Despite the constraints, commended
staff for making the available events successful and utilizing sponsors to provide free refreshments.
Expressed hope that expanded summer programming, including more concerts and movies, can return
next year.

Recognized: A Zoom call from Mario Dominguez SG Resident - Raised concerns about the City’s current
cooling-center policy, which requires temperatures to reach 95 degrees for three consecutive days.

REQUEST FOR ITEMS ON FUTURE AGENDAS – None

ADJOURNMENT - At 7:41 p.m. Chair Flores asked for a motion to adjourn.
M/S/C: Secretary Esquivel/Commissioner Trujillo

Respectfully submitted:

Cynthia Esquivel, Secretary
Parks & Recreation Commission
